items.title: ECHO: A Locally-Deployable Agentic Health Assistant with Temporal Memory, Safety Guardrails, and Speech Assessment
items.abstract: ECHO is a locally-deployable health assistant for chronic care that uses an agentic chatbot with temporal memory and clinical tools. Its core contribution lies in its robust safety system, combining a fast rule-based layer with a GNN for accurate clinical intent classification, ensuring secure and effective long-term health management.

items.title: Learning Globally Reusable Skills for Coding Agents
items.abstract: This paper introduces GSE, a framework for improving LLM coding agents by evolving skills globally. Unlike local updates, GSE uses a Skill Relation Graph to model inter-skill relationships and cluster-based consolidation to abstract reusable capabilities, enhancing generalization and preventing overfitting. This approach leads to more robust and adaptable coding agents.

items.title: TRAJDEBUG: Tracing Error Lifecycle to Identify Critical Failures in Long-Horizon Agent Trajectories
items.abstract: TrajDebug is a framework designed to pinpoint the root cause of failures in long, complex trajectories generated by LLM-based agents. It addresses challenges of scattered evidence and multiple local errors by using multi-granularity history compression and evidence-based identification. The core contribution is tracing the "error lifecycle" to determine which initial error ultimately leads to the final failure, enabling more effective debugging.
items.figure_caption: Critical error detection requires grounding errors in long-range context and distinguishing the failure-responsible error from multiple coexisting errors.

items.title: A Six-Dimensional Taxonomy of Post-Training Adaptation Techniques with Applications in AI Governance
items.abstract: This paper introduces a six-dimensional taxonomy to systematically categorize and understand the diverse landscape of post-training adaptation techniques in machine learning. Its core contribution lies in providing a unified framework that clarifies distinctions between similar methods and illustrates the evolution of adaptation strategies across different model types. This taxonomy aims to improve comparability and comprehension of how models are modified after initial training, with applications in AI governance.

items.title: The Bitter Lesson of Tool Calling
items.abstract: This paper introduces Programmatic Tool Calling (PTC), a method that allows LLMs to use tools by invoking them as typed Python scripts, enabling natural chaining and parallelization. Empirically, PTC matches or surpasses traditional JSON tool calling across most tested models, significantly improving performance for some, especially under parallel execution scenarios. The core contribution is demonstrating PTC's effectiveness as a more flexible and powerful tool-use paradigm for LLMs.
items.figure_caption: Overview of the two primary paradigms evaluated. In JSON tool calling , the model emits JSON tool-call objects via the API. In programmatic tool calling , it writes a Python script using typed stubs; the agent loop executes it in a subprocess. A filesystem-discovery condition is included as a secondary reference point.

items.title: Training-Free Token-Level Steering for LLM Personalized Co-Writing
items.abstract: This paper introduces SteerWrite, a training-free framework for personalized LLM co-writing. Its core method achieves token-level steering without gradient updates, making it efficient for small datasets and specialized domains. SteerWrite's contribution lies in enabling personalized co-writing with reduced human editing effort, outperforming existing methods across various benchmarks.

items.title: Benchmarking the Benchmarks: Evaluating Benchmarks for Conversational Agents
items.abstract: This paper introduces a novel, reference-free framework that leverages LLM judges to evaluate the quality of conversational agent benchmarks. The core method assesses benchmark consistency, complexity, and policy coverage, providing actionable diagnostics of weaknesses. The contribution lies in offering a practical and scalable approach to identify and improve unreliable benchmarks, ultimately leading to more robust evaluations of task-oriented conversational agents.

items.title: Contextual Information Policy Optimization for Search Agents
items.abstract: This paper introduces Contextual Information Policy Optimization (CIPO), a novel reinforcement learning framework for search agents. CIPO addresses the problem of agents relying too heavily on internal knowledge by explicitly rewarding the grounding of their reasoning in retrieved external evidence at each step. This evidence-oriented approach aims to improve the reliability and efficiency of multi-step reasoning in knowledge-intensive tasks.
items.figure_caption: Illustrative case for the same question. Prior-driven reasoning uses retrieval mainly to confirm a parametric guess, whereas evidence-driven reasoning lets retrieved evidence change the next action.

items.title: DASH: Divergence-Adaptive Supervision Horizons for On-Policy Self-Distillation of Reasoning Models
items.abstract: This paper introduces DASH, a novel on-policy self-distillation method for improving reasoning in language models. DASH addresses the issue of sparse rewards in reinforcement learning by adaptively weighting token-level supervision based on the temporal context of divergence between a teacher and student model. This divergence-adaptive supervision allows for more effective learning by prioritizing corrections based on the history of discrepancies.

items.title: EnvACE: Internalizing Environment Dynamics via World Rehearsal for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: EnvACE trains large language model agents for complex tool use by replacing costly environment interactions with "world rehearsal." The agent learns by alternating between generating tool calls and simulating the environment's responses to those calls, internalizing environment dynamics directly into its parameters. This approach creates an agent world model that improves decision-making and achieves strong performance across multiple benchmarks.
items.figure_caption: Comparison of three agent rollout paradigms: real-environment rollout, external-simulator rollout, and EnvACE world rehearsal. Existing approaches obtain environment responses from external sources, whereas EnvACE internalizes environment responses within the policy through world rehearsal.

items.title: Evaluating Investment Logic in Large Language Models: A Real-World Benchmark Towards Personalzied Financial Agents
items.abstract: This paper argues that current evaluations of financial LLMs fail to capture personalized investment competence. They introduce \textsc{InvestLogicBench}, a novel benchmark using real-world investor data to evaluate LLMs based on their reasoning and decision-making process, not just profit. This allows for a more nuanced assessment of an agent's ability to act consistently with an investor's profile and market conditions.
items.figure_caption: The “Capabilities-Performance Paradox” in financial domain. (Left) Cumulative equity curves between autonomous LLM agents and human expert proxies in a 7-week live U.S. stock trading competition. DeepSeek-V3 achieved the highest cumulative return, significantly outperforming the S&P 500 benchmark, while models like GPT-5 and Claude-Sonnet-4.5 demonstrated lackluster performance in seizing opportunities. Key market inflection points highlight periods where expert logic diverged from model behavior. (Right) Comparative analysis between Foundation Aptitude Scores and Real-World Cumulative Returns. It suggests that superior performance on general benchmarks fails to reliably transfer into financial analytical acumen or effective real-world trading execution.

items.title: FinEvo-Bench: A Longitudinal Benchmark for Self-Evolving Agents in Professional Financial Workflows
items.abstract: FinEvo-Bench is a new benchmark designed to evaluate self-evolving financial agents by testing their ability to learn and improve across a series of interconnected, real-world financial tasks. Its core method involves a longitudinal design with 120 tasks across six financial domains, each with institution-defined procedures and quality rubrics. The key contribution is its ability to measure how agents retain and leverage experience from previous tasks to enhance performance on subsequent ones, unlike existing benchmarks that evaluate tasks in isolation.
items.figure_caption: Overview of FinEvo-Bench. Left: 20 business scenes across six financial domains, comprising 120 tasks. Right: an example Stock Technical Analysis task with its natural-language request and six input files.

items.title: HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization
items.abstract: This paper introduces HarnessOpt-Bench, a novel benchmark designed to evaluate Large Language Models (LLMs) in their ability to optimize "harnesses" – the surrounding code, prompts, and tools that enable LLMs to act as agents. The core method involves an LLM-based optimizer iteratively improving a given harness based on graded feedback and a fixed evaluation budget, aiming to maximize performance gains over an initial seed harness. The key contribution is providing a standardized protocol for measuring this crucial, yet previously unquantified, capability of LLMs in agentic systems.
items.figure_caption: Trusted execution for held-out harness optimization. The optimizer can write only the target agent’s harness. It can read the evaluation results and the target task data but not modify them. The optimizer receives per-case development traces and aggregate validation metrics, while test cases and scores remain inaccessible behind the trusted evaluation server. Each candidate is evaluated in isolated, unprivileged sandboxes, and every model call, both the optimizer’s own and the evaluations’, passes through a gateway that enforces model allow-lists and per-scope budgets. The test partition is evaluated only after the optimizer nominates a final candidate. Because held-out data, provider credentials, and budget enforcement are absent from the optimizer’s sandbox, these restrictions are properties of the execution environment rather than instructions the optimizer is expected to follow.

items.title: Poli-Bias: Understanding and Measuring Large Language Model Biases in International Political Conflicts
items.abstract: This paper introduces Poli-Bias, a novel counterfactual framework to measure political bias in LLMs. It systematically swaps country identities in legally equivalent conflict scenarios to reveal subtle disparities in framing and reasoning. Poli-Bias decomposes these differences into five dimensions, offering a nuanced understanding of how LLMs exhibit unequal treatment across various geopolitical contexts.
items.figure_caption: LLMs may treat legally equivalent conflict scenarios differently based on the countries involved.

items.title: When History Lies: Evaluating and Improving Tool Use under Misleading Multi-Turn Histories
items.abstract: This paper addresses how misleading multi-turn histories can cause tool-using AI agents to make incorrect decisions, even when they possess the correct underlying policy. The authors introduce a benchmark with synchronized "Original," "Polluted," and "Oracle" history views to isolate failure points. They then propose a method called "ours" that trains a student agent to overcome polluted histories by transferring knowledge from an oracle-conditioned teacher.
items.figure_caption: Overview of the problem, benchmark, and method. (A) An example in which a failed historical interface call precedes the current request while leaving the task state and gold action unchanged. (B) The synchronized Polluted, Original, and Oracle State views in ContextPollute-Bench , together with the evaluated Call and Answer decisions. (C) Oracle-OPD training with polluted-context student rollouts and Oracle-conditioned teacher supervision on the same prefixes. Deployment uses only the trained student and ordinary interaction history.

items.title: MetaboLLM: a metabolomics-specialized large language model for biochemical knowledge integration and predictive metabolite graph construction
items.abstract: MetaboLLM is a specialized large language model designed to integrate fragmented metabolomics knowledge by adapting general LLMs through continual pretraining, fine-tuning, and structured retrieval. Its core contribution is enabling the construction of predictive metabolite graphs (MetaboLLM-GIN) from generated biochemical descriptions, which significantly improves patient-level prediction tasks like stress hyperglycemia and hormone-regimen classification compared to existing methods.

items.title: On-Policy Self-Distillation without Any Supervision
items.abstract: This paper introduces Unsupervised On-Policy Self-Distillation (U-OPSD), a novel method for improving large language models without external supervision. U-OPSD leverages internal consistency by generating multiple outputs, identifying confident errors through majority voting, and then distilling a corrected version into the model's incorrect generations. This approach allows LLMs to self-correct their confidently held mistakes, leading to consistent performance gains across various benchmarks.
items.figure_caption: Comparison between OPSD / SDFT with ground-truth solution or ICLs (left), SDPO with rich feedback from the environment (middle) and our u-OPSD without any supervision.

items.title: SAGA: Score-Weighted Adaptive Generation Alignment for Low-Resource Nordic Language Models
items.abstract: SAGA is a novel framework that uses dependency parser outputs instead of human annotations to optimize low-resource language models. It converts parser judgments into preference pairs, combines parser quality with lexical diversity for rewards, and filters low-information pairs. This approach significantly improves grammatical quality in Nordic languages without costly human labeling.
items.figure_caption: Parser-derived supervision replaces human preference labels: the incorrect case ( Ég ) fails dependency parsing, whereas the correct case ( Mig ) is accepted, providing a preference signal without human annotation.

items.title: RP-OPSD: Reasoning-Pivot-Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation for Multilingual Reasoning Transfer
items.abstract: This paper introduces RP-OPSD, a method to improve multilingual reasoning transfer in LLMs. It guides on-policy self-distillation by focusing on "reasoning pivots" – critical decision points in the reasoning process. By using the distributional shift between teacher views with and without an English reference, RP-OPSD effectively anchors the distillation process to enhance cross-lingual reasoning capabilities.
items.figure_caption: Motivation of reasoning-pivot-guided transfer. Surface variants can preserve the same reasoning state, while pivot drift corrupts downstream reasoning. RP-OPSD uses the distribution gap between the solution-conditioned view q t + q_{t}^{+} and the ablated view q t − q_{t}^{-} to identify reasoning-sensitive tokens. The Frence CoT means ”So we multiply 4 by 3, which makes 12”.

items.title: AV-AIVAT: 74x Cheaper Agent Evaluation with Certified Anytime-Valid Stopping in Imperfect-Information Games
items.abstract: This paper introduces AV-AIVAT, a method for evaluating the relative strength of two agents in imperfect-information games. It combines a variance reduction technique (AIVAT) with anytime-valid stopping rules (Confidence Sequences) to achieve significantly cheaper evaluations. The core contribution is enabling evaluations to stop as soon as sufficient evidence is gathered, while maintaining statistical guarantees, reducing costs by up to 74x compared to traditional methods.
items.figure_caption: Run-level heterogeneity in the 15 HUNL evaluations. Each point is one configuration. Dashed lines mark cross-run medians, and the cross in the EB panel denotes the one ratio censored because the raw stream failed to cross in most reshufflings.

papers.title: A Six-Dimensional Taxonomy of Post-Training Adaptation Techniques with Applications in AI Governance
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a six-dimensional taxonomy to systematically categorize and understand the diverse landscape of post-training adaptation techniques in machine learning. Its core contribution lies in providing a unified framework that clarifies distinctions between similar methods and illustrates the evolution of adaptation strategies across different model types. This taxonomy aims to improve comparability and comprehension of how models are modified after initial training, with applications in AI governance.

papers.title: The Bitter Lesson of Tool Calling
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Programmatic Tool Calling (PTC), a method that allows LLMs to use tools by invoking them as typed Python scripts, enabling natural chaining and parallelization. Empirically, PTC matches or surpasses traditional JSON tool calling across most tested models, significantly improving performance for some, especially under parallel execution scenarios. The core contribution is demonstrating PTC's effectiveness as a more flexible and powerful tool-use paradigm for LLMs.
papers.figure_caption: Overview of the two primary paradigms evaluated. In JSON tool calling , the model emits JSON tool-call objects via the API. In programmatic tool calling , it writes a Python script using typed stubs; the agent loop executes it in a subprocess. A filesystem-discovery condition is included as a secondary reference point.

papers.title: Training-Free Token-Level Steering for LLM Personalized Co-Writing
papers.abstract: This paper introduces SteerWrite, a training-free framework for personalized LLM co-writing. Its core method achieves token-level steering without gradient updates, making it efficient for small datasets and specialized domains. SteerWrite's contribution lies in enabling personalized co-writing with reduced human editing effort, outperforming existing methods across various benchmarks.

papers.title: Benchmarking the Benchmarks: Evaluating Benchmarks for Conversational Agents
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel, reference-free framework that leverages LLM judges to evaluate the quality of conversational agent benchmarks. The core method assesses benchmark consistency, complexity, and policy coverage, providing actionable diagnostics of weaknesses. The contribution lies in offering a practical and scalable approach to identify and improve unreliable benchmarks, ultimately leading to more robust evaluations of task-oriented conversational agents.

papers.title: Contextual Information Policy Optimization for Search Agents
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Contextual Information Policy Optimization (CIPO), a novel reinforcement learning framework for search agents. CIPO addresses the problem of agents relying too heavily on internal knowledge by explicitly rewarding the grounding of their reasoning in retrieved external evidence at each step. This evidence-oriented approach aims to improve the reliability and efficiency of multi-step reasoning in knowledge-intensive tasks.
papers.figure_caption: Illustrative case for the same question. Prior-driven reasoning uses retrieval mainly to confirm a parametric guess, whereas evidence-driven reasoning lets retrieved evidence change the next action.

papers.title: DASH: Divergence-Adaptive Supervision Horizons for On-Policy Self-Distillation of Reasoning Models
papers.abstract: This paper introduces DASH, a novel on-policy self-distillation method for improving reasoning in language models. DASH addresses the issue of sparse rewards in reinforcement learning by adaptively weighting token-level supervision based on the temporal context of divergence between a teacher and student model. This divergence-adaptive supervision allows for more effective learning by prioritizing corrections based on the history of discrepancies.

papers.title: EnvACE: Internalizing Environment Dynamics via World Rehearsal for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: EnvACE trains large language model agents for complex tool use by replacing costly environment interactions with "world rehearsal." The agent learns by alternating between generating tool calls and simulating the environment's responses to those calls, internalizing environment dynamics directly into its parameters. This approach creates an agent world model that improves decision-making and achieves strong performance across multiple benchmarks.
papers.figure_caption: Comparison of three agent rollout paradigms: real-environment rollout, external-simulator rollout, and EnvACE world rehearsal. Existing approaches obtain environment responses from external sources, whereas EnvACE internalizes environment responses within the policy through world rehearsal.

papers.title: Evaluating Investment Logic in Large Language Models: A Real-World Benchmark Towards Personalzied Financial Agents
papers.abstract: This paper argues that current evaluations of financial LLMs fail to capture personalized investment competence. They introduce \textsc{InvestLogicBench}, a novel benchmark using real-world investor data to evaluate LLMs based on their reasoning and decision-making process, not just profit. This allows for a more nuanced assessment of an agent's ability to act consistently with an investor's profile and market conditions.
papers.figure_caption: The “Capabilities-Performance Paradox” in financial domain. (Left) Cumulative equity curves between autonomous LLM agents and human expert proxies in a 7-week live U.S. stock trading competition. DeepSeek-V3 achieved the highest cumulative return, significantly outperforming the S&P 500 benchmark, while models like GPT-5 and Claude-Sonnet-4.5 demonstrated lackluster performance in seizing opportunities. Key market inflection points highlight periods where expert logic diverged from model behavior. (Right) Comparative analysis between Foundation Aptitude Scores and Real-World Cumulative Returns. It suggests that superior performance on general benchmarks fails to reliably transfer into financial analytical acumen or effective real-world trading execution.

papers.title: FinEvo-Bench: A Longitudinal Benchmark for Self-Evolving Agents in Professional Financial Workflows
papers.abstract: FinEvo-Bench is a new benchmark designed to evaluate self-evolving financial agents by testing their ability to learn and improve across a series of interconnected, real-world financial tasks. Its core method involves a longitudinal design with 120 tasks across six financial domains, each with institution-defined procedures and quality rubrics. The key contribution is its ability to measure how agents retain and leverage experience from previous tasks to enhance performance on subsequent ones, unlike existing benchmarks that evaluate tasks in isolation.
papers.figure_caption: Overview of FinEvo-Bench. Left: 20 business scenes across six financial domains, comprising 120 tasks. Right: an example Stock Technical Analysis task with its natural-language request and six input files.

papers.title: HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization
papers.abstract: This paper introduces HarnessOpt-Bench, a novel benchmark designed to evaluate Large Language Models (LLMs) in their ability to optimize "harnesses" – the surrounding code, prompts, and tools that enable LLMs to act as agents. The core method involves an LLM-based optimizer iteratively improving a given harness based on graded feedback and a fixed evaluation budget, aiming to maximize performance gains over an initial seed harness. The key contribution is providing a standardized protocol for measuring this crucial, yet previously unquantified, capability of LLMs in agentic systems.
papers.figure_caption: Trusted execution for held-out harness optimization. The optimizer can write only the target agent’s harness. It can read the evaluation results and the target task data but not modify them. The optimizer receives per-case development traces and aggregate validation metrics, while test cases and scores remain inaccessible behind the trusted evaluation server. Each candidate is evaluated in isolated, unprivileged sandboxes, and every model call, both the optimizer’s own and the evaluations’, passes through a gateway that enforces model allow-lists and per-scope budgets. The test partition is evaluated only after the optimizer nominates a final candidate. Because held-out data, provider credentials, and budget enforcement are absent from the optimizer’s sandbox, these restrictions are properties of the execution environment rather than instructions the optimizer is expected to follow.

papers.title: Poli-Bias: Understanding and Measuring Large Language Model Biases in International Political Conflicts
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Poli-Bias, a novel counterfactual framework to measure political bias in LLMs. It systematically swaps country identities in legally equivalent conflict scenarios to reveal subtle disparities in framing and reasoning. Poli-Bias decomposes these differences into five dimensions, offering a nuanced understanding of how LLMs exhibit unequal treatment across various geopolitical contexts.
papers.figure_caption: LLMs may treat legally equivalent conflict scenarios differently based on the countries involved.

papers.title: When History Lies: Evaluating and Improving Tool Use under Misleading Multi-Turn Histories
papers.abstract: This paper addresses how misleading multi-turn histories can cause tool-using AI agents to make incorrect decisions, even when they possess the correct underlying policy. The authors introduce a benchmark with synchronized "Original," "Polluted," and "Oracle" history views to isolate failure points. They then propose a method called "ours" that trains a student agent to overcome polluted histories by transferring knowledge from an oracle-conditioned teacher.
papers.figure_caption: Overview of the problem, benchmark, and method. (A) An example in which a failed historical interface call precedes the current request while leaving the task state and gold action unchanged. (B) The synchronized Polluted, Original, and Oracle State views in ContextPollute-Bench , together with the evaluated Call and Answer decisions. (C) Oracle-OPD training with polluted-context student rollouts and Oracle-conditioned teacher supervision on the same prefixes. Deployment uses only the trained student and ordinary interaction history.

papers.title: MetaboLLM: a metabolomics-specialized large language model for biochemical knowledge integration and predictive metabolite graph construction
papers.abstract: MetaboLLM is a specialized large language model designed to integrate fragmented metabolomics knowledge by adapting general LLMs through continual pretraining, fine-tuning, and structured retrieval. Its core contribution is enabling the construction of predictive metabolite graphs (MetaboLLM-GIN) from generated biochemical descriptions, which significantly improves patient-level prediction tasks like stress hyperglycemia and hormone-regimen classification compared to existing methods.

papers.title: On-Policy Self-Distillation without Any Supervision
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Unsupervised On-Policy Self-Distillation (U-OPSD), a novel method for improving large language models without external supervision. U-OPSD leverages internal consistency by generating multiple outputs, identifying confident errors through majority voting, and then distilling a corrected version into the model's incorrect generations. This approach allows LLMs to self-correct their confidently held mistakes, leading to consistent performance gains across various benchmarks.
papers.figure_caption: Comparison between OPSD / SDFT with ground-truth solution or ICLs (left), SDPO with rich feedback from the environment (middle) and our u-OPSD without any supervision.

papers.title: SAGA: Score-Weighted Adaptive Generation Alignment for Low-Resource Nordic Language Models
papers.abstract: SAGA is a novel framework that uses dependency parser outputs instead of human annotations to optimize low-resource language models. It converts parser judgments into preference pairs, combines parser quality with lexical diversity for rewards, and filters low-information pairs. This approach significantly improves grammatical quality in Nordic languages without costly human labeling.
papers.figure_caption: Parser-derived supervision replaces human preference labels: the incorrect case ( Ég ) fails dependency parsing, whereas the correct case ( Mig ) is accepted, providing a preference signal without human annotation.

papers.title: RP-OPSD: Reasoning-Pivot-Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation for Multilingual Reasoning Transfer
papers.abstract: This paper introduces RP-OPSD, a method to improve multilingual reasoning transfer in LLMs. It guides on-policy self-distillation by focusing on "reasoning pivots" – critical decision points in the reasoning process. By using the distributional shift between teacher views with and without an English reference, RP-OPSD effectively anchors the distillation process to enhance cross-lingual reasoning capabilities.
papers.figure_caption: Motivation of reasoning-pivot-guided transfer. Surface variants can preserve the same reasoning state, while pivot drift corrupts downstream reasoning. RP-OPSD uses the distribution gap between the solution-conditioned view q t + q_{t}^{+} and the ablated view q t − q_{t}^{-} to identify reasoning-sensitive tokens. The Frence CoT means ”So we multiply 4 by 3, which makes 12”.

papers.title: AV-AIVAT: 74x Cheaper Agent Evaluation with Certified Anytime-Valid Stopping in Imperfect-Information Games
papers.abstract: This paper introduces AV-AIVAT, a method for evaluating the relative strength of two agents in imperfect-information games. It combines a variance reduction technique (AIVAT) with anytime-valid stopping rules (Confidence Sequences) to achieve significantly cheaper evaluations. The core contribution is enabling evaluations to stop as soon as sufficient evidence is gathered, while maintaining statistical guarantees, reducing costs by up to 74x compared to traditional methods.
papers.figure_caption: Run-level heterogeneity in the 15 HUNL evaluations. Each point is one configuration. Dashed lines mark cross-run medians, and the cross in the EB panel denotes the one ratio censored because the raw stream failed to cross in most reshufflings.
